prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer stands above a floor (~1.3–1.6 m below) next to a vertical wooden wall on the upper-left that drops steeply from ~0.3 m near the head down to the floor. In the lower foreground (~0.3–0.8 m away), the wearer's own legs and arms are within immediate reach, with the right hand raised very close to the lens (~0.2–0.3 m) in frame 1 before lowering to ~0.5–0.7 m in frames 2–5 as the left hand raises a smartphone to ~0.4–0.5 m in frames 4–5. Ahead and to the upper-right on the floor (~1.0–1.5 m from the wearer, and ~0.3–0.6 m from the wearer's knees), an upright orange bucket and a crouching second person (facing down and leftward toward a floor drain, never looking at the wearer) are within each other's arm's reach (~0.2–0.4 m apart). In frame 1 the wearer's raised right arm partly occludes the bucket, and across frames 1–5 the crouching person shifts slightly further toward the upper-right edge while reaching into the bucket in frame 5. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height of the rim and interior of the orange bucket, the steep perspective plane of the wooden wall, and the elevation of the wearer's hands above the floor, though it blurs small floor tools (red bit case, fittings, yellow tool on the left tarp) into the dark floor plane.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a sparse subset of foreground regions across the 5 frames: in frame 1 it merges the camera wearer's raised right arm (~0.2–0.5 m away) and the crouching second person (~1.0–1.4 m ahead in the upper-right, facing down and left away from the wearer) into overlapping pink and brown 'person' masks where the arm occludes the bucket and worker. In frames 2–5, it detects the round orange bucket on the middle-right floor (~1.0–1.3 m from the wearer, within the crouching worker's reach and just beyond the wearer's lower legs) as a circular mask, while capturing the wearer's lower body and hands in frame 4 (~0.4–0.8 m) alongside the held 'cell phone' (~0.4–0.5 m on the left) and a partial 'person' mask for the crouching worker at the top edge in frames 3 and 4. Across the sequence, the masks show the wearer's right arm dropping out of the upper-right view after frame 1, the phone appearing in the wearer's left hand in frame 4 and tilting leftward in frame 5, and the bucket shifting slightly right relative to the frame. While segmentation sharply delineates the boundary between the held phone and the wearer's fingers in frame 4 and tracks the circular rim of the bucket better than a quick glance at the cluttered RGB floor, it is highly unreliable here: it misclassifies the orange bucket as a 'frisbee' in frames 2–5, mislabels the phone as a 'remote' in frame 5, merges the two distinct people in frame 1, and completely misses the wearer's legs in frames 2, 3, and 5 as well as the wall and all small floor tools.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the 5 frames, detecting only a single magenta 21-keypoint hand skeleton in frame 4 corresponding to the camera wearer's left hand holding the smartphone at ~0.4–0.5 m in front of the torso, slightly left of centre and ~0.3 m above the left knee. Those magenta keypoints show the wrist at the bottom-left and the four fingers and thumb curving rightward and upward around the back and left edge of the phone, within immediate reach of the wearer's right hand (~0.1 m to the right). Even though the RGB strip shows the wearer's lower body and right arm in all 5 frames (~0.2–0.8 m away) and a second person crouching on the upper-right floor (~1.0–1.5 m away, facing downward and left toward a floor opening and reaching into the orange bucket in frame 5), no yellow body skeletons or other hand skeletons are rendered in any frame. In frame 4, the detected left-hand skeleton provides precise finger articulation on the rear of the phone that is partly occluded by the phone body in RGB. However, the map is largely unreliable across the strip due to severe top-down self-occlusion, steep egocentric viewing angles, and partial framing that cause complete detection failures for both people's bodies and all other visible hands in frames 1–5.
